definition.simple: The powerhouse of the cell. It takes the food we eat and turns it into energy the cell can use.
definition.academic: Double-membrane-bound organelles found in most eukaryotic organisms that generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.

examples: Muscle cells have lots of mitochondria because they need a massive amount of energy to help you move.

common_misconceptions: Mitochondria make energy out of nothing. (False: They convert glucose from food into ATP, they don't 'create' energy from nothing due to the laws of physics).
ai_context.tutor_hint: Mitochondria are amazing—they actually have their own separate DNA and ribosomes, meaning they can make some of their own proteins!
